## The main point
The meeting was a status review of outstanding Technology Governance (TGOV) deliverables, led by Jennifer Camarro, with Danielle T. Benjamin, Robert T. Garnett, James Haskins, and Brandon M. O'Hara participating; Neal was absent. Jennifer reported the process is roughly 66% complete but stalled across several categories, and asked Danielle and James to each take ownership of categories to relieve her, since she has been managing follow-up alone without a project manager. Danielle agreed to take more than one if needed; Jennifer decided to keep ESG and procurement herself and distribute the rest, though no specific assignments were finalized by the end. ESG is a hard blocker — Jennifer has submitted three versions and the reviewing team appears to be tracking an older one — and enterprise security architecture cannot move until the current ESG is approved. On the MSA with vendor Estrada, Jennifer said two rounds of red lines are complete and it is close to legal review, but James Dodson redirected it to a different reviewer; Jennifer and Rob agreed to tag-team that item, and James Haskins offered his daily Teams contact with the Estrada team (Jay and Lauren). Jennifer flagged a possible future question about whether the chart tool will be hosted in Elevance's or Estrada's environment; Brandon said Estrada prefers their own environment and suggested starting there for the pilot, and Jennifer said she agreed for the pilot phase.

## Presented, no challenge recorded
- Jennifer Camarro: status is unchanged from what was shared the day before; the process is approximately 66% complete.
- Jennifer Camarro: the ESG work is complicated by two components — digital quality measure and year-round chart collection — which can be treated independently or as a connected entity.
- Jennifer Camarro: the MSA has gone through two rounds of red lines with minimal back-and-forth on either side; no hard disagreement exists, only completion remains.
- Jennifer Camarro: the chart tool can be deployed two ways — within Elevance's own Snowflake/AWS environment or hosted within Estrada's walls as vendor-hosted software.

## Open questions
- What deliverables are outstanding and who is waiting on what? (raised by Danielle T. Benjamin)
- How should the two ESG components be sequenced or combined? (raised by Jennifer Camarro)
- What procurement agreement is needed to unblock data sharing and testing before the full MSA is in place? (raised by Jennifer Camarro)
- How should the chart tool be deployed for Elevance — within Elevance's environment or Estrada's? (raised by Jennifer Camarro)

## Where people stand
- Danielle and James providing additional support on outstanding categories: Danielle T. Benjamin supports — "Sure. Works for me."
- Host chart tool within Estrada's walls / start pilot in Estrada's environment, migrate later: Brandon M. O'Hara supports — "I think their preference is their environment… it might be worth starting in their environment"; Jennifer Camarro supports if the goal is a fast pilot — "If we want to get a pilot up and running, that's the way to go."
- Proposed, no reaction recorded: proceed with one ESG component ahead of the other; pilot data-sharing agreement (not full MSA) to open pipes; set up FTP for pilot data exchange; licensed UAT environment for parallel YRDC testing; deploy chart tool within Elevance's own Snowflake/AWS with an Estrada contractor as admin; and 1 more.

- ESG team is tracking an older submission and has not replied to the most current one; Jennifer has followed up three times. (Jennifer Camarro)
- Enterprise security architecture review cannot begin until the final ESG is approved. (Jennifer Camarro)
- Enterprise Architecture has not told Prasad Edathil what he needs to complete on the architecture solution design task. (Jennifer Camarro)
- Responsible AI team is not responding to follow-ups. (Jennifer Camarro)
- MSA is pending legal review and must be in place before data sharing or a pilot can start; it has now been redirected to a different reviewer. (Jennifer Camarro, James Haskins)
